description:
FILED s473t5b (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 3 (op/ CHECK 2): 71 of
t/op/packagev.t's 79 remaining blessed fail rows -- the residue after #1587
made `eval "package NAME VERSION"` work at all.  (The other 8 are #1640, the
v-string $VERSION.)

perl has ONE version grammar with TWO strictness levels, and t/op/packagev.t
drives both from one __DATA__ table (37 value rows x 7 assertions):

  * `package NAME VERSION;` and `package NAME VERSION { }` accept only a
    STRICT version, and the tokenizer refuses anything else AT COMPILE TIME:
      package withversion 01;        Invalid version format (no leading zeros)
      package withversion .1;        ... (0 before decimal required)
      package withversion 1.;        ... (fractional part required)
      package withversion 1.02_03;   ... (underscore)
      package withversion 1.2.3;     ... (dotted-decimal versions must begin with 'v')
      package withversion v1.2;      ... (dotted-decimal versions require at least three parts)
      package withversion v1.2345.6; ... (maximum 3 digits between decimals)
      package withversion bar;       ... (non-numeric data)
    PCL accepts every one of them and runs on (probed: `eval "package
    withversion 1.2.3; 1"` answers 1 with $@ empty; perl answers undef).
    58 rows, each a `like($@, qr/$match/)`.

  * `version->new("STR")` accepts only a LAX version and dies with the same
    message family for the rest:
      version->new("1.a")   Invalid version format (fractional part required)
      version->new("1_")    ... (underscore)
      version->new("v")     ... (dotted-decimal versions require at least three parts)
      version->new("bar")   ... (non-numeric data)
    PCL's `lib/version.pm` shim never asks: `new` stores the string as given,
    so `version->new("bar")` succeeds and stringifies as "bar".  13 rows.

THE SHIM ALREADY HAS THE PREDICATES.  `lib/version.pm` carries `$STRICT` and
`$LAX` (the two regexes, transcribed from perl's version::regex) and
`is_strict`/`is_lax` -- and the file's `... should pass/fail STRICT/LAX regex`
rows PASS today.  So the LAX half is: `new` asks `is_lax` and dies with
perl's message.  What it needs beyond that is the REASON, because the test
matches on it ("non-numeric data", "fractional part required", "underscore",
"dotted-decimal versions require at least three parts", "maximum 3 digits
between decimals", "no leading zeros"); perl's own reasons come from
version::vpp::scan_version and are structural, so they are derivable from the
string -- MEASURE them from real perl rather than guessing, one probe per
__DATA__ row.

PROBE THE CASE IT WOULD BREAK (feedback_probe_the_breaking_case): the same
file's column 4 calls `version->new(V)` UNQUOTED, so the argument is a
V-STRING (`version->new(v1.2.3)`), which is NOT lax-matching as text.  perl's
new() special-cases a vstring argument.  In PCL today a v-string literal is
its own source TEXT (#1640), which is why those rows pass now -- a naive
`is_lax` gate would break them the moment #1640 is fixed, so the vstring arm
belongs in the same change.

THE STRICT HALF IS THE PARSER, NOT THE SHIM (CLAUDE.md 9a): `package NAME
VERSION` is a statement, and `Pl::Parser2::_pkg_version_forms` (s484a) is the
one reading of its shape.  perl refuses at COMPILE time, so in a string eval
the refusal lands in $@ -- the ruled perl-shaped refusal shape -- and in file
mode it is a transpile-time die.  A version that IS strict must stay
untouched; `package Foo;` with no version must stay untouched.

BAR: the __DATA__ table itself is the acceptance table (37 values x the 7
assertions); re-run t/op/packagev.t and splice; the full sweep is
NON-OPTIONAL for the `lib/` half (s377 rule) and `use version` is loaded by
`lib/experimental.pm`, so a wrong die there reaches every file that loads it.
subject: perl's VERSION GRAMMAR is absent in both strictness levels: `package NAME <bad version>` is accepted where perl refuses at compile time (58 rows) and `version->new("bad")` is accepted where perl dies (13 rows) -- t/op/packagev.t's residue after #1587
